name: airlock
description: Boundary attestation primitive. Proves what crossed the model boundary, which upstream artifacts influenced it, and what claim level was earned. `assemble` builds a deterministic prompt payload plus prompt provenance, `verify` checks a model request against the policy and emits an airlock manifest, `explain` summarizes a manifest, and `witness` queries the local receipt ledger. `doctor`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` are read-only discovery surfaces.

options.description: Print the airlock manifest JSON Schema and exit 0

commands.name: assemble
commands.description: Assemble a deterministic prompt payload plus prompt provenance from policy-approved inputs.

options.name: policy
options.description: Boundary policy YAML file

options.name: input
options.description: Input JSON artifact; repeat for multiple upstream artifacts

options.name: system_prompt
options.description: Optional UTF-8 system prompt file included in provenance

options.name: boundary_mode
options.description: Boundary exposure mode: ANNOTATED (default) or TELEMETRY_ONLY

options.name: out
options.description: Path to write prompt_payload.json

options.name: provenance_out
options.description: Path to write prompt_provenance.json

options.name: not_crossed_out
options.description: Optional path to write not_crossed.json (airlock.not_crossed.v1): every input field that did not cross the boundary, by path, source hash, value hash and reason; values are never stored

options.name: prior_receipt
options.description: Chained turn: the gate receipt (airlock.gate.v1) that recorded the earlier response. Must be an admitted 2xx exchange naming a matched manifest, and its response_hash must equal the hash of --response. The receipt is unsigned JSON, so this link is only as strong as the file's custody. Requires --response, --response-adapter and --prior-manifest

options.name: response
options.description: Chained turn: the provider response body from the earlier turn, exactly as received (JSON, not a stream). Its text and tool calls enter the prompt as MODEL_OUTPUT under prior_turn

options.name: response_adapter
options.description: Chained turn: the provider that produced --response, openai_responses or anthropic_messages

options.name: prior_manifest
options.description: Chained turn: the earlier turn's manifest. Its hash must equal the receipt's matched_manifest_hash. The new prompt's chain link records that hash and the next turn_index, and the manifest verify writes for it is airlock.v0.4

options.name: tool_result
options.description: Chained turn: a tool result answering a tool call in --response, as TOOL_USE_ID=PATH (PATH is a UTF-8 text artifact embedded verbatim as TOOL_RESULT). The strict claim needs the policy's declared_tool_results to list the blake3 hash of its exact bytes; an undeclared tool result is admitted but caps the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT

options.name: no_witness
options.description: Skip ambient witness ledger recording

commands.name: verify

options.description: not_crossed.json from `airlock assemble --not-crossed-out`; refused unless it belongs to this run (same policy, prompt payload and boundary mode). Its entries are copied into the manifest; without it the manifest records no negative inventory

commands.name: send
commands.description: Verify a request and transmit it to a model endpoint in one process, then record what crossed. Builds the request from the assembled prompt with the adapter named in --transport, judges it with the same code as `verify`, POSTs exactly the RFC 8785 canonical bytes that request_payload_hash covers and bytes_crossed measures, and writes an airlock.v0.3 manifest whose `transmission` member records the endpoint host, bytes, hashes, status and latency. Only the request body is attested: headers are not hashed or recorded, and HTTP(S)_PROXY is honoured, so the manifest names the endpoint, not a proxy. Redirects are never followed. The API key is read from the environment variable the transport file names and is never written anywhere. https is required except to a loopback host. Exit 0: the exchange completed and a response was received (any HTTP status). Exit 1: the achieved claim was below --require-claim (default RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT) and nothing was sent. Exit 2: a refusal; for E_TRANSPORT, detail.sent says whether the body may have reached the endpoint.

options.name: policy
options.description: Boundary policy YAML used during assembly

options.name: prompt

options.name: transport
options.description: JSON transport declaration: adapter, model, url, api_key_env, and optionally params, headers, auth_header, timeout_seconds (default 120, max 900), max_response_bytes (default 32 MiB, max 256 MiB) and, for generic_json, the JSON pointers. May not set credential or framing headers

options.name: out
options.description: Path to write airlock_manifest.json. A pre-send manifest (self_attested, no transmission) is written first and replaced after the exchange

options.name: request_out
options.description: Path to write the exact request bytes that were sent (owner-only). It is the manifest's replay_ref

options.name: response_out
options.description: Path to write the response body, only when it was received completely (owner-only)

options.name: require_claim
options.description: Minimum claim needed to send: BOUNDARY_FAILED, RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT or STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY. Defaults to RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT, so a request that failed the boundary check is sent only with an explicit --require-claim BOUNDARY_FAILED

options.name: not_crossed
options.description: not_crossed.json from `airlock assemble --not-crossed-out`; same rules as `verify`

options.name: no_sign
options.description: Write the manifest without an Ed25519 signature. By default send signs with the key from `airlock keygen` and refuses when there is none

options.name: no_witness
options.description: Skip ambient witness ledger recording

commands.name: keygen
commands.description: Generate the Ed25519 key pair that `verify` signs manifests with, under ~/.cmdrvl/secrets/airlock/ (ed25519.key owner-only, ed25519.pub). Never overwrites an existing key; prints the public key and fingerprint, never the secret.

commands.name: verify-manifest
commands.description: Check the Ed25519 signature on an airlock.v0.3 or airlock.v0.4 manifest. Exit 0 when valid; a refusal (exit 2) with reason unsigned, signature_mismatch, fingerprint_mismatch, unsupported_manifest_version, unsupported_algorithm or malformed_signature otherwise.

options.name: pubkey
options.description: Public key file (hex, as airlock keygen writes it); default ~/.cmdrvl/secrets/airlock/ed25519.pub

commands.name: chain
commands.description: Check the chain of turns a manifest belongs to. `chain verify` walks back from the given manifest to turn 0 (a manifest with no chain member) and checks every link: the chain member agrees with the manifest version; with --pubkey, a signed manifest's signature (unsigned is reported, not refused); the prior manifest named by prior_manifest_hash is in --manifest-dir and turn_index is one more than its index; the turn's prompt provenance is there, carries the same link and names exactly one admitted response hash; and with --receipt-dir, a gate receipt names that response and the prior manifest. Files in the directories are matched by content, never by name. Exit 0 with a JSON report when every link holds. A chain that does not hold is a refusal (exit 2, E_BAD_MANIFEST) with detail.reason one of chain_shape, signature_invalid, prior_manifest_not_found, turn_index_mismatch, provenance_not_found, provenance_chain_mismatch, model_output_hash_missing, model_output_hash_ambiguous, receipt_not_found or receipt_response_mismatch; the manifest on the command line can also be refused as not_a_manifest or unsupported_manifest_version. A gate receipt is unsigned: this shows that the hashes of the manifests, provenance files and receipts agree with one another, not who produced any of them. Read-only: writes nothing and records nothing in the witness ledger.

arguments.name: manifest
arguments.description: verify only: airlock_manifest.json of the newest turn to check

options.name: manifest_dir
options.description: verify only: directory holding the earlier turns' manifests and their prompt_provenance.json files (*.json files directly in it)

options.name: receipt_dir
options.description: verify only: directory of gate receipts. Without it the receipts are not checked, and the report says so

options.name: pubkey
options.description: verify only: public key file (hex, as airlock keygen writes it). Signed manifests in the chain are checked with it; without it signatures are not checked

commands.name: witness
commands.description: Query the local witness ledger (`query`, `last`, `count`) and check its hash chain (`verify`) without recording witness entries. An empty result (no ledger, no records, or a filter that matches nothing) is success: exit 0, with `[]` from `query --json`, `{"count":0}` from `count --json` and `null` from `last --json`. `verify` walks the airlock entries and checks that each `prev_hash` is the blake3 of the previous airlock line: exit 0 when the chain is intact (or the ledger has no airlock entries), exit 1 with status CHAIN_BROKEN when a link does not hold, or HEAD_MISMATCH when `--expect-head` is given and the chain's head differs. The chain is a local tamper hint, not a proof: it does not detect entries removed from the end or a ledger rewritten whole with recomputed hashes, and covers airlock entries only. A ledger or filter that cannot be read or parsed, or a malformed `--expect-head`, is a refusal (exit 2).

options.name: json
options.description: Emit machine-readable JSON

options.name: expect_head
options.description: verify only: fail with HEAD_MISMATCH unless the chain head is this blake3:<64 hex> value, one an earlier run printed and you kept where the ledger's writers cannot reach

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Inspect read-only CLI health without reading run artifacts or touching witness state; every JSON form is a cmdrvl.doctor.v1 report. `doctor --json` is mode health; `doctor capabilities --json` is mode capabilities (its `contract` is this document); `doctor triage --json` is mode triage (with next_actions). Exits 0 healthy, 1 unhealthy. Deprecated aliases kept for compatibility: `doctor health [--json]`, `doctor --robot-triage` and top-level `--robot-triage` (same document as `doctor triage --json`).

options.name: json
options.description: Emit doctor health as JSON

options.name: robot_triage
options.description: Deprecated alias of `doctor triage --json`

0.meaning: VERIFY_PASS: the command completed and any --require-claim was met; also a healthy doctor, every read-only discovery surface, any `witness query|last|count`, including one with an empty result, a `witness verify` whose chain is intact, and a `send` whose exchange completed with a response (any HTTP status) (a verify that earns BOUNDARY_FAILED without --require-claim still exits 0 with an honest manifest verdict)

1.meaning: VERIFY_PARTIAL: verification completed but the achieved claim fell below --require-claim (for `send`, nothing was sent); also `doctor` reporting an unhealthy state (an error finding); also `witness verify` reporting CHAIN_BROKEN or HEAD_MISMATCH

2.meaning: REFUSAL or CLI/usage error: a structured refusal envelope on stdout (bad policy, input, prompt, request, provenance or manifest, missing file, witness or internal error), or a clap usage error

refusals.message: Boundary policy failed to parse or validate
An input artifact or argument is malformed or unusable
prompt_payload.json is malformed or not a prompt airlock assembled
The transport-wrapped model request is malformed or unsupported
prompt_provenance.json is malformed or inconsistent with the prompt

refusals.action: Re-run `airlock verify` to regenerate the manifest

refusals.message: A required file does not exist
The witness ledger could not be read or queried
refusals.action: Check EPISTEMIC_WITNESS and the ledger path, or use `--no-witness`

refusals.message: airlock send could not complete the exchange with the endpoint
refusals.action: Read refusal.detail.sent: false means the request body was never written, true means it may have reached the endpoint; the manifest at --out records which
Report this with the refusal detail

env_vars.name: HTTPS_PROXY
env_vars.description: `send` honours HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and NO_PROXY (and their lowercase forms) like any HTTP client. The manifest records the endpoint host, not the proxy the bytes went through

env_vars.name: NO_COLOR
env_vars.description: Disable ANSI color in human output (airlock emits none when piped)

env_vars.name: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
env_vars.description: Unix seconds. Pins the `verify` manifest timestamp so identical inputs give a byte-identical manifest. A set but malformed value is an E_BAD_INPUT refusal, not a fallback to the clock. Witness records keep the real wall clock.

env_vars.name: TERM
env_vars.description: TERM=dumb disables ANSI color in human output

side_effects.notes: send is the one command that transmits a model request: it POSTs to the url in the --transport file, reads the API key from the environment variable that file names (api_key_env), and writes --out, --request-out and optionally --response-out. assemble and verify write the paths given by --out/--provenance-out; gate writes receipts under --out-dir and forwards through its loopback listener. These commands append witness records unless --no-witness is set; explain, witness, doctor, capabilities, robot-docs and verify-manifest are read-only. keygen writes ed25519.key and ed25519.pub under ~/.cmdrvl/secrets/airlock/ (never overwriting) and records nothing in the witness ledger; verify reads that key to sign unless --no-sign is set.
